A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same VisionPAD research. All 11 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2 support comparison, including readable figures, tables and equations. V2 adds Appendices A–C; v1 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 report original detection, occupancy and map-segmentation experiments, component ablations, data-efficiency results and qualitative examples.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and adds Gaussian-parameter ablations, resource measurements, an augmented UniPAD comparison and a qualitative case study.

M1.justification: The proposed Gaussian decoder, opacity filtering, velocity-guided voxel warping, photometric consistency and weighted losses remain unchanged in Section 3. The appendix documents existing implementation choices and evaluates variants without establishing a revision to VisionPAD's proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate nuScenes 3D detection, Occ3D semantic occupancy and map segmentation. The added ablations, profiling and visualization remain within this coverage; no new dataset, task, domain or distinct input scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds UniPAD augmented with voxel velocity estimation and photometric consistency as an evaluated comparator alongside unmodified UniPAD and VisionPAD. Comparator membership in Tables 1–4 is unchanged. NeRF-MAE is added only as a citation.

E3.justification: V2 introduces targeted parameter controls, including alternative Gaussian offsets, scales, rotations and anchor counts. Appendix B also introduces memory and latency evaluation at matched 360 × 640 rendering resolution on one A100 GPU. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; the equal-epoch clarification supplies additional documentation.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and data-efficiency study, v2 tests Gaussian parameterization and anchor-count sensitivity, rendering efficiency, filtering costs and transfer of the motion/photometric components to UniPAD. Appendix C adds a case study examining detection errors and occupancy representation. These substantially expand the questions investigated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new experimental entries retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figure 4 retain their numerical results. V2 adds Tables 5–8, anchor-count findings and qualitative error observations. For example, Table 6 reports 1973 MB/900 ms for UniPAD-C versus 134 MB/70 ms for VisionPAD, while Table 7 newly reports 25.6 NDS/23.3 mAP for augmented UniPAD. These are additional comparisons rather than version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds explicit sigmoid-bounded mathematical definitions for Gaussian means and scales in Equations 11–12, previously described only at a higher level. The existing rendering and loss equations remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof. The added standard metric formulas are explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: Gaussian-based vision-only pre-training, self-supervised motion and geometric learning, and improved performance across three downstream tasks. The added experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning anchored means, learnable scales and fuller photometric supervision, plus discussion of false positives, excavator orientation errors and occupancy's computational tradeoff. The new fixed-parameter discussion needs qualification: Table 5 shows fixed rotation slightly lowers NDS but raises mAP from 26.5 to 26.7.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B disclose warping pseudocode, pose transformation, the 1/12-second frame interval, offset factor 0.25, Gaussian scale bounds [0.1, 0.5] and profiling hardware. Table 1 newly identifies camera-only UniPAD results as the authors' implementations. These extend the existing training recipe without establishing changes to its settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds NeRF-MAE, reference 15, to the masked-modeling discussion. The other cited works and the central positioning against depth-supervised rendering approaches remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely retained. V2 adds acknowledgements and organized supplementary sections, corrects limited terminology and typographical errors, and clarifies captions and implementation wording. It does not extensively rewrite the existing exposition.

P2.justification: V2 substantially extends the displayed evidence with Tables 5–8, Algorithm 1 and the multi-panel detection/occupancy Figure 7. Figures 1–2 receive revised rendering labels and Table 1 gains attribution and modality explanations. The existing data-efficiency plot and qualitative Figures 3, 5 and 6 retain their content.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful additional support through matched-resolution resource measurements, the augmented UniPAD control and implementation disclosures. The case study also makes limitations more explicit. These strengthen an otherwise retained empirical study, although profiling covers one stated setup and some new interpretations exceed the mixed evidence, particularly the fixed-rotation results in Table 5.
